docs.text: Description ¶ Dataverse command-line interface. It uses the Dataverse API and in some cases direct access to the Dataverse database. The commands are implemented using dans-dataverse-client-lib . Some of the more complex commands are documented below. Common features of dv dataverse-create-dataset and dv dataset-edit-metadata ¶ The commands dv dataverse-create-dataset and dv dataset-edit-metadata work in the same way: they process one dataset specified on the command line, or a batch of datasets specified in a CSV input file ( --input-file , -i ), one row per dataset. This section describes what they have in common; the sections on the individual commands describe their specific columns and options. Input file and columns ¶ The columns of the input file fall into several categories. Which of these apply depends on the command: Dataset identifier ( dv dataset-edit-metadata only) Preconditions ( dv dataset-edit-metadata only) Processing instructions Field values Column names are case-insensitive. Avoiding conflicts between special columns and fields If a metadata field has the same name as one of the non-field columns of the command (e.g., pid ), prefix the name of the non-field column with * , e.g., *pid . The prefix is optional otherwise. If both *pid and pid are present, the first is the special column and the second is a metadata field. Field names must not start with * . The *result and *message columns in the report always have the * preempting any possible conflicts with field names. Field types ¶ The names of the field value columns depend on the metadata blocks that are available. A primitive field or controlled vocabulary field is specified simply by the field identifier, e.g., myField . If multiple values are to be added, the field identifier is indexed, e.g., myField[1] . myField[2] , etc. A compound field is specified by the field identifier of the parent field, followed by a dot and the name of the child field, e.g., myField.myChildField . Note that in many cases the name of the child field refers to the parent field by convention, e.g., authorName , but you still have to prefix it with the parent field identifier, e.g., author.authorName . If multiple values of a compound field are to be added, the parent field identifier is indexed, e.g., myField[1].myChildField , myField[2].myChildField , etc. Default values ¶ Values for the columns can also be given as command line options, which can be combined with --input-file . In that case they provide default values for the corresponding columns: If the CSV file has no column of that name, the command line value is used for every row. If the column exists, the command line value is used for the rows where the cell is empty or blank. A non-blank cell always takes precedence. If neither a column value nor a command line option is given, the setting is not applied (unless the command defines a default for it). Field values can have defaults too: <column name>=<value> arguments can be combined with --input-file . They work the same way: a column that is missing from the CSV file gets the value for every row, and for an existing column the value is used for the rows where the cell is empty or blank. How blank cells in field columns are interpreted otherwise is specific to the command. Note that you will need to enclose the whole argument in quotes if the value contains spaces, or if the name has an index, e.g., 'myField[1]=longer value with spaces' . Running without CSV input file Since you can provide defaults for all the columns, it is also possible to run the commands without a CSV input file. This can be useful when testing. Other options ¶ --timeout (for example 30s , 2m ; seconds if no unit is given) is not a column; it applies to the wait for publication of each dataset. --wait-between-rows (same format as --timeout , default no wait; only allowed together with --input-file ) is not a column either; it sets the time to wait after each processed row, except the last one, e.g., to throttle the load on the Dataverse instance. --reports-dir overrides the location of the report . Report ¶ When running with a CSV input file, a report will be written to a file in the directory configured in editMetadata.reportsDir in .dv.yml . The --reports-dir option can be used to override this location. The report contains a copy of each line, with the column names exactly as in the input (so an optional * is kept or absent as it was), plus the columns for default values that were not in the input file, so that the effective input is visible (blank cells in the input are filled with the default value), plus the extra columns *result and *message , which always have the * . The columns are ordered as: identifier ( pid , databaseId or datasetId ), *result , *message , the processing instruction columns (e.g., *expectedState ), and finally the metadata field columns. When running without a CSV input file, the report is written to the standard output. The *result column contains one of: OK : the row was processed successfully FAILED : an error occurred while processing the row SKIPPED : the row was skipped because a precondition was not met dv dataverse-create-dataset ¶ Creates one dataset, or a batch of datasets, in a collection. It uses the Create a dataset endpoint. The common features described above apply. Only the metadata blocks enabled for the target collection can be used, and the fields that Dataverse requires must be provided. Columns ¶ alias - the alias of the collection in which to create the dataset. Default: the value of --alias , or root if that is not specified either. A non-blank cell takes precedence over the command line option. publish - whether to publish the dataset after creation: yes , or no (synonym: leave-draft ). Default: the value of --publish , or no . A newly created dataset is always published as version 1.0, so there is no choice of version type. Any other column is a metadata field value (see Field types ). dv dataset-edit-metadata ¶ For bulk changes on the metadata of multiple datasets in a Dataverse instance, you can use dv dataset-edit-metadata . This command uses the Edit metadata endpoint, which allows you to add or replace metadata fields in a dataset. For typical usage, the command takes a CSV file as input. The common features described above apply. Columns ¶ Dataset identifier datasetId - the database ID or PID of the dataset, a PID must contain the protocol, e.g., doi:10.5072/FK2/123456 pid - the persistent identifier of the dataset, which must start with a protocol label, e.g., doi:10.5072/FK2/123456 databaseId - the database ID of the dataset, consisting of digits only The input file must contain exactly one of these three columns; they are mutually exclusive. Each row must have a value in that column; there is no default identifier (the --datasetId , --pid and --databaseId options cannot be used together with an input file). Use pid or databaseId instead of datasetId if you want the identifier to be validated against its expected format. When no input file is used, exactly one of the three options is required. Preconditions expectedState - the expected state of the dataset version to be edited, one of draft , released , deacessioned or a negation of one of those, e.g., not released . The default precondition is not deaccessioned . expectInReview - whether the dataset is expected to be in review: yes or no . The default is no expectation. =<fieldId> - the expected current value of the field with identifier <fieldId> , e.g., =title , =subject[2] or =author[1].authorName . Before making any changes, the command checks that the field in the latest version has exactly this value (case-sensitive, surrounding whitespace in the cell ignored). If not, the row is skipped. An empty cell means the field is expected to have no value. For a multivalued field without index, the first value is checked. On the command line, use e.g. =title=Old title . Processing instructions publishVersion - whether to publish the dataset after editing, one of minor , major or leave-draft (no publication action is attempted) or no (a synonym for leave-draft ). N.B. If the dataset was a draft before editing, publication is only attempted if this was explicitly expressed in expectedState . versionNote - a note to set on the draft version before publication. This involves a separate API call and requires the version note to be enabled in Dataverse. (See Enabling version notes .) replace - whether to replace existing values or add to them: yes or no Field values An empty cell leaves the field unchanged if replace is no , and removes the field's value(s) if replace is yes . To leave a field unchanged while replace is yes , put !skip in the cell. If the value !skip must literally be stored in a field, choose another skip code with the --skip-code option (default !skip ).

docs.text: Installation ¶ Currently, this project is built as an RPM package for RHEL8/Rocky8 and later. The RPM will install the binaries to /opt/dans.knaw.nl/dd-dv-cli and the configuration files to /etc/opt/dans.knaw.nl/dd-dv-cli . Building from source ¶ Prerequisites: Java 21 or higher Maven 3.8.7 or higher RPM Steps: git clone https://github.com/DANS-KNAW/dd-dv-cli.git cd dd-dv-cli mvn clean install
